Maintenance Report — MNT-0157-005

Asset: WELL-0157 (NE-08 Well 157, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: separator Work started: 04 Aug 2023 08:00 · Finished: 07 Aug 2023 23:00 · Well stopped for this job: 87 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price, Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0157-0041 on 2023-08-03 Report written: 08 Aug 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the separator high-level alarm stayed on. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0157-0041 showed the wellhead at 36.6 °C with the air at 35.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The level controller had failed. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Controller float and switch failure.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 8 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Isolated and depressurised the separator.
  2. Replaced the level controller.
  3. Calibrated the controller and tested the dump valve.

Summary of the fix: replaced level controller.

Testing and return to service

Cycled the separator three times; level control worked correctly. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0157-010

Asset: WELL-0157 (NE-08 Well 157, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 17 May 2024 08:00 · Finished: 17 May 2024 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0157-0081 on 2024-05-16 Report written: 18 May 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0157-0081 at 13:45 on 2024-05-16 found crude oil on the pad: about 8.6% of the pad area, estimated 1.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 6.0 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 384 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 307 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.0 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0157-010 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.85% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0157-018

Asset: WELL-0157 (NE-08 Well 157, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 19 Sep 2025 08:00 · Finished: 01 Oct 2025 06:00 · Well stopped for this job: 286 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0157-0148 on 2025-09-18 Report written: 03 Oct 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0157-0148 showed the wellhead at 34.4 °C with the air at 29.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 10 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
